causeOfPainAndProblems.title: CAUSE OF PAIN AND PROBLEMS
causeOfPainAndProblems.author: Maharishi
causeOfPainAndProblems.description: According to the developed characters in the body and mind, whatever waves emerge from the deeds, thoughts and experiences which are conflicting with the natural functioning order within and without, those waves result in contamination of the genetic center. Such contaminated imprints create problems and pains in life. Once they are imprinted and stored, they will persist for a long time, over several generations. These undesirable imprints can be selectively neutralized by expiation, superimposition, and dissolution. Everyone has the potential to do this by proper practice and moral behavior.

keyPoints.point1: Contamination of the genetic center results in problems and pain.
keyPoints.point2: Imprints can persist for several generations.
keyPoints.point3: Selective neutralization is possible through proper practices.

betterToBeHealthyThanWealthy.title: Better to be healthy than wealthy
betterToBeHealthyThanWealthy.author: Maharishi

intro.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Physical exercises are very important for mankind. In the olden days, people did not give importance to physical exercise. The reason was that they had enough physical labour. So, they were able to maintain a healthy body and did not care much about the physical exercises. Even women were taught classical dances, and for men, sports were encouraged. What does this prevalence and usage show?

They show indirectly that exercises are a must for everyone. But due to rapid scientific development, this physical labour and sports have been reduced. Regulated physical labour is essential to maintain the health of the body. To digest food well and to expel remainders and impurities from the body properly, physical labour is an intrinsic need.

Most women feel shy to do exercises. When one practices waking up early in the morning and doing exercises regularly, this shyness will vanish. Many housewives say that their household work is exercise for them. It might be, but the same kind of work engages only a portion of the body. Instead, the whole body should be maintained in a healthy condition. For this, a systematic series of exercises is necessary.

plantsAndAnimals.title: Plants and Animals Do Exercises
paragraphs: Even one-sensed plants, by means of wind, shake their leaves and branches, performing exercises. Five-sensed animals twist their bodies, jump, walk, and do exercises. But only man, who is gifted with the sixth sense, does not care about his own body. Health is better than wealth. It is better to be healthy than wealthy. No matter how rich a man may be, he can never be happy if he is not healthy or if he does not do systematic physical exercises. It is necessary for us to develop and maintain harmony in all aspects.

When the body is kept in a healthy state, harmony between the body and life will be well maintained. Prevention is better than cure. Therapy is of two kinds: curative and preventive. The preventive method is superior. It is better to take preventive measures instead of suffering and then resorting to curative methods.

So, the maintenance of one's own body and mind is the duty of man. He must live, fulfill his duties, and enjoy the world only through his body and soul. The physical body is the principal instrument of duty; it is a natural gift to man. Taking care of this natural gift is essential for all other achievements.

speciality.title: Specialty of Maharishi’s Simplified Physical Exercises
paragraphs: The systems of physical exercises taught by our Guru, Vethathiri Maharishi, have preventive as well as curative values. They develop immunity in the body. These exercises are suitable for all climates, countries, and sections of the human community, including men, women, and children (above 8 years). The specialty of these exercises is that no limb or internal organ of the practitioner is subjected to any strain.

The exercises are based on scientific truths and follow scientific lines. They can be performed with extreme ease, and the movements are smooth and graceful. The practitioner should focus on perfecting the movements of the limbs and body.
The time required to complete these exercises is relatively short, about 30 minutes, and no mechanical aids or devices are necessary. They involve no monetary expenditure at all.

conclusion.title: Conclusion
paragraphs: Physical exercises are very important for mankind. In the olden days, people did not give importance to physical exercise. The reason was that they had enough physical labour, which allowed them to maintain a healthy body without focusing much on physical exercises. Even women were taught classical dances, and sports were encouraged for men. This prevalence shows that exercises are necessary for everyone.

However, due to rapid scientific development, physical labour and sports have diminished. Regulated physical labour is essential for maintaining health. To digest food well and expel impurities from the body, physical labour is an intrinsic need.

Most women feel shy to do exercises. By waking up early and practicing exercises regularly, this shyness will disappear. Many housewives may claim that their household work serves as exercise, but such work engages only specific portions of the body. A systematic series of exercises is necessary for the overall health of the body.
conclusion.quote: By the Grace of the Omniscient, my physical form and shape was structured to completion, starting from the origin of a single droplet of the sexual vital fluid. O, how do tiny little cells in cooperative endeavor stage endless miracles in the metabolic routine!

theThirdEyeAThousandPetalsInOurBrain.title: The Third Eye & A Thousand Petals in Our Brain
theThirdEyeAThousandPetalsInOurBrain.author: Maharishi

paras.para1: The sixth centre is the Agna chakra having its seat in the region between the eyebrows and is related to our life-force. It is linked with the Pituitary gland. The word 'Agna' means control, administration. This centre controls the sensual activities.
paras.para2: This is called the 'third eye' which is an addition to the sensual perceptions and abilities. Here only, the sixth sense is increasing more and more to expose your potential fully. Hence, it is called the intellectual point to control the senses.
paras.para3: If you divide the brain into three parts, the front part is the intellectual part, having control over the sense organs. The middle part is the lobe of wisdom, the function of which is to increase and transform man from material consciousness to God consciousness.
paras.para4: The rear part is the lobe of universal secrets. It is also connected with the Pineal gland and therefore the universal secrets are revealed. The Pineal gland is the master gland for psychic functions.

section2.title: A Thousand Petals in Our Brain

paras.para1: 'Thuria centre' (Brahmarandhra) is called as crown centre. 'Thuria' means 'highest peak'. The Brahmarandhra or the Thuria centre is linked with the Pineal gland. The Pineal provides direct connection to the mind and also, it is the gland for psychic functions to adjust the focusing of the mind to anything or to any frequency. When you meditate on the Pineal gland, the Pituitary gland also gets the benefit.
paras.para2: This centre is also called 'Sahasrahara' or thousand petal lotus. In the East, our forefathers had found that our brain has one thousand regional valves. Each petal or valve has some specific function. When all the thousand regional valves are activated to function, man's intellect will increase sharply and by this development of knowledge, he will be able to fix his mind with any level of universal function or the universal force.
paras.para3: Also practicing Thuria Meditation brings the mind to frequencies very near to no frequency. Brahma means God State which has no frequency at all. The top of the head is called 'Brahma-randhra'. That is this belief which coined the word Brahma-Randhra. Brahma means god and randhra means way or gate.

paras.para1: All actions will create appropriate imprints in man. The Law of Nature reflects such imprints again and again in the mind and the body and involves the man in the same actions and brings out proper results as pain and pleasure sensation or peace and satisfaction. Such repetition of the same type of actions makes the imprints deeper and stronger and conditions the personality appropriately.
paras.para2: I am telling very often to superimpose the imprints of sinful actions by virtuous deeds. There is a common notion that even good actions will cause lengthening of the birth cycle, so as to get the happiness of enjoying the results of good deeds. I have to clear this point more elaborately.

section2.title: Purpose of Man's Existence and Imprints

paras.para1: Man's existence has a purpose. His consciousness has to be developed to its perfection. Before the realisation of the purpose of the birth, he was conditioned in his personality by sensual limitations. Thereby, three impurities, namely:
paras.para2: Ego, imprints of sins and undue attachment to men and material have been formed in him.
paras.para3: When the consciousness is developed, the imprints will be purified. When the imprints are cleared or balanced, the consciousness will automatically develop. Any of these two or both could be achieved only by the virtuous way of life. Any action which will help to purify the impurities develops good deeds.

paras.para1: Repetition of the same type of actions makes the imprints deeper and stronger and conditions the personality appropriately.
paras.para2: It is the duty of man to do only virtuous deeds to reach his goal. Any action which would increase the aforesaid three impurities or obstruct, delay, or divert the journey of the consciousness in its development towards perfection is termed sinful and negative.
paras.para3: So, good actions are only positive and purposeful to reach the goal of human beings. They are to be practiced and maintained to enjoy harmony, happiness, and peace.
paras.para4: Only negative actions should be avoided. If any such action had already been done, those imprints should be superimposed by the imprints of good actions.

paras.para1: Some people are thinking that good actions also will cause new births to enjoy the benefits or the fruits of the good actions. Only this concept I deny.
paras.para2: Good actions lead one to reach the goal, cutting the length of the birth cycle. What one should do is good deeds, and that is duty. If it is done, that will help one to reach the goal. Good deeds also get imprinted.
paras.para3: But, those imprints when reflected, involve one to do the same good deeds and thus help him to reach the goal.

paras.para1: The imprint of Karma loses its reflecting force in one hundred and forty years calculated for seven generations (twenty-year period for one generation). But, if within this period, the imprint is revived by some thought or action, that will be in force for a further period of one hundred and forty years from the time of revival.
paras.para2: Therefore, there are more chances for endless continuance of all the imprints unless they are balanced by a proper method of neutralization which has three types: 1) expiation, 2) superimposition or 3) dissolution.

paras.para1: The Akashic records once created last forever and cannot be erased. Once imprinted in the universal consciousness, they exist permanently. However, imprints in the physical body can be superimposed and changed. In the Super-consciousness, everything from the beginning up to the present moment stands recorded.

Yoga is a system to make a man 'a real man' to enjoy life happily, peacefully, and blissfully. The purpose of man's life is noble—it is to develop consciousness to its fullest. Yoga aligns the method of living with the purpose of life. To achieve this goal quickly and successfully, one must understand the purpose of life and lead life systematically. Following a way of life with an understanding of its purpose is Yoga.
paras.para2: Man's life operates in three dimensions: self, society, and Nature. Therefore, one must understand the Law of Nature, the value of society, its constitution, and the sentiments of its people. Additionally, a person must know all aspects of their own personality—body, mind, and soul—before they can lead a life of responsibility.

paras.para1: Yoga has been classified into four stages: Bhakthi Yoga, Karma Yoga, Raja Yoga, and Gnana Yoga. Bhakthi Yoga is essential for the innocent and ignorant in the early stages of life. As a person matures, Karma Yoga becomes necessary. Raja Yoga is for achieving satisfaction and peace, and finally, Gnana Yoga is required to lead others toward enlightenment.
paras.para2: Bhakthi Yoga teaches people to cultivate good habits from childhood, guided by elders. Karma Yoga requires serving society with an understanding of one’s responsibility, while Raja Yoga focuses on the development of consciousness. Finally, Gnana Yoga is practiced to lead others and sacrifice personal knowledge for the welfare of society.

section3.title: Yoga and the Law of Nature

paras.para1: Yoga means aligning one's will with Nature. There should never be conflict between will and Nature, as the resources of Nature are abundant. When one's will clashes with Nature, pain, misery, and problems arise, obstructing life's progress toward its ultimate goal. Such conflicts harm not only the individual but also the society in which they live.
paras.para2: Living in harmony with Nature through the yogic way of life allows one to avoid such problems and live in peace and bliss.

paras.para1: In Bhakthi Yoga, which is essential during the early years of life, there are three key processes: learning language, learning production skills, and learning to form good habits that do not result in pain to oneself or others. These processes together are called education. During this period, children must follow the path shown by parents and teachers.

As one matures, they must render their services to society in return for the benefits and material comforts received. This is Karma Yoga. However, Karma Yoga is not separate from Bhakthi Yoga but should be practiced alongside it.

When a person questions the purpose of life and the reason behind their actions, they are ready to practice Raja Yoga. This stage involves developing consciousness so that the senses are subordinate to it. Raja Yoga requires understanding the laws of Nature and the self, which consists of four elements: body, mind, soul, and the Almighty. Raja Yoga also includes psychic practices to focus the mind on the life force, enabling one to uncover the secrets of life and achieve harmony between body, mind, and soul.

After mastering Bhakthi Yoga, Karma Yoga, and Raja Yoga, some individuals progress to Gnana Yoga. This stage involves complete dedication to the welfare of society, sacrificing personal gains and knowledge for the greater good.

Physical well-being is essential for both spiritual development and overall health. Maintaining proper circulation of blood, heat, and air in the body is critical. To achieve this, one must regulate food habits, sexual indulgence, work, rest, and the use of thought force. Daily physical exercises help prevent mal-circulation and are part of yoga.
paras.para2: In addition to physical health, maintaining a peaceful and balanced state of mind is crucial. Without mental well-being, the physical body deteriorates.

paras.para1: To achieve harmony between the body and soul, it is important to maintain good blood circulation and practice meditation, introspection, sublimation, and perfection. When the mind is peaceful and in equilibrium, the life force operates in harmony, enabling mental and physical health.
paras.para2: By maintaining harmony in oneself, one can create harmony in the family and society as well. In this way, yoga helps foster peace and well-being across all aspects of life.

paras.para1: Everyone has five kinds of duties: to maintain personal well-being, to maintain harmony with friends, to maintain harmony with relatives, to contribute to society, and to maintain harmony at work. These duties should be fulfilled without causing conflict with the other responsibilities. Maintaining one’s health is not selfishness; it is part of one’s duty to society.
paras.para2: Understanding one's role and responsibilities in life brings satisfaction and helps individuals contribute positively to society. By living in harmony with others and performing one's duties with awareness, one contributes to the greater good.

paras.para1: In life, understanding one's role and responsibilities leads to peace and satisfaction. Yoga provides a systematic way to cultivate this understanding, ensuring that every action is beneficial to both oneself and society. By following the yogic path, one can lead a harmonious, happy, and successful life.

introduction.summary: The Akash particles are seen as the repository of all the secrets of nature and the source of all sciences. They play a crucial role in understanding the universe and its functioning.

panchaBhoodasAndAkashParticles.description: The universal field is composed of five elements or Pancha Bhoodas (elements): Akash, Air, Fire, Liquid, and Solid. These elements are associations of Absolute Space and energy particles. The proportion of energy particles and space varies in each element.

elements.description: The subtlest element, primarily composed of energy particles.
The densest of all the Bhoodas.

panchaTanmatras.description: Akash particles, through their interactions and waves, manifest in five perceptible forms called Pancha Tanmatras.

tanmatras.description: The first and primary result of Akash particle interactions.
Predominantly perceived in Air, with pressure latent.
The dominant result in Fire, where pressure and sound are latent.
Predominantly perceived in Liquid, with the other Tanmatras latent.
Predominantly perceived in Solid, with the other Tanmatras latent.

interactionsAndClashes.description: The interactions between waves from Akash particles and other Bhoodas create the five Tanmatras. These interactions include clashes, reflections, refractions, and are responsible for the perception of pressure, sound, light, taste, and smell.

lifeForceAndSensations.description: Living beings are made up of the Pancha Bhoodas and radiate their own Tanmatras due to the circulation and functions of the life force.

sensations.description: When a living being comes into contact with an object, the Tanmatras from the object influence the life force, causing sensations.
Consciousness inherent in life force particles distinguishes the degrees of Tanmatras and senses these differences through comparisons.

universalLawsOfEnergyAndInteraction.description: The life force is subject to acceleration or aggravation based on atmospheric disturbances. Every object radiates waves of its natural character, and the interaction between these waves results in changes in other objects.
universalLawsOfEnergyAndInteraction.consciousness: The consciousness in the life force helps in distinguishing and comparing the degrees of forces through Tanmatras.

akashParticlesAsRepositoriesOfSecrets.description: Every energy particle records all movements, waves, and interactions. These records are what condition the character and functioning of the particle.

conclusionForResearchersAndTruthSeekers.message: Understanding the principle of Akash particles is crucial for scientists and truth seekers. Research into Akash particles is essential as it leads to enlightenment and eventual emancipation of humanity. These particles contain the core truths of the universe.

introduction.title: INTRODUCTION

definition.postponeDeath: postponement of death until the time one wishes

introduction.summary: Kaya Kalpa focuses on rejuvenating the body and postponing death through natural exercises and spiritual energy management.

earlyDevelopment.summary: Ever since man started curing illness, prevention of illness and prolonging life have been major objectives in cultural evolution. Philosophers and healers have sought to understand the secrets of nature and the aging process.

buddhistInfluence.summary: Six centuries before Christ, Lord Buddha identified the need for a system to alleviate suffering from disease, old age, and death, but the secrets of aging remained elusive for centuries.

siddhaAlchemists.summary: Between the 10th and 15th centuries, South Indian alchemists known as 'Siddhas' developed methods to prolong life. Their teachings on rejuvenation and death defiance are scattered throughout writings, but are difficult to interpret today.

earlyInquiry.summary: In his youth, Maharishi began asking questions about life, God, and suffering. Although his initial studies of Siddha texts on Kaya Kalpa were confusing, his later experiences in Kundalini Yoga and self-realization allowed him to fully understand the science and practical applications.

studyAndPractice.summary: After years of studying Ayurveda, Siddha, and Homeopathy, Maharishi rediscovered the principles of Kaya Kalpa. With his newfound understanding, he began practicing and teaching these methods to others.

teachingKayaKalpa.summary: Maharishi now teaches Kaya Kalpa to hundreds of people yearly, with reported success in enhancing physical vitality, curing illnesses, and obtaining spiritual benefits.

spiritualBenefits.title: SPIRITUAL BENEFITS
spiritualBenefits.summary: Kaya Kalpa helps transmute sexual energy into spiritual energy, leading to the enlightenment of consciousness. It transforms emotional moods into spiritual awareness, fostering behavior aligned with welfare and happiness.

physicalBenefits.title: Physical Benefits
physicalBenefits.overallHealth: Improves overall health and rejuvenates the body.

nervousSystemToning.name: Toning the nervous system
nervousSystemToning.description: This exercise helps the body withstand the aging process.

ojasBreath.name: Ojas Breath
ojasBreath.description: This practice recycles sexual vital fluid to rejuvenate the body and postpone death.

learningStructure.summary: Kaya Kalpa is taught in two sittings of 1.5 hours each. The first sitting covers the science of body chemistry, while the second teaches the practical exercises.

eligibility.summary: Anyone after maturity can learn Kaya Kalpa, with no prior spiritual or meditation experience required. It can be practiced alongside other spiritual practices.

moderation.summary: Success in Kaya Kalpa is dependent on observing moderation in food, work, rest, sex, and use of thought force.

personalOath.summary: Practitioners are required to take an oath not to teach Kaya Kalpa to others without the permission of the teacher.

sexualVitalFluid.summary: Kaya Kalpa helps thicken and increase the stock of sexual vital fluid, which strengthens the life force and bio-magnetism, prevents old-age troubles, and enhances sexual potency.

spiritualEnergy.summary: Sexual energy is transmuted into spiritual energy, fostering spiritual awareness and improving the practitioner's character and personality.

geneticImprovement.summary: Through consistent practice, genetic improvement for healthier and more intelligent offspring can be achieved.

conceptionControl.summary: Conception can be controlled at will when one partner has successfully practiced Kaya Kalpa for a sufficient period.

conclusion.summary: Kaya Kalpa helps maintain physical and mental health, furthers spiritual development, and rejuvenates the body to withstand aging. Maharishi is satisfied with its results and believes it can solve many problems of humanity.

introduction.quote: There are some people who do not know anything, through them also the Nature teaches us lessons.
introduction.author: Maharishi

rolesOfTeacherAndStudent.summary: Every person in the world is both a teacher and a student. By learning and teaching, the world becomes united. Elders guide those who are less experienced, while Nature teaches us lessons even through those who do not know anything.

learningFromChildren.summary: Nature's teachings are present in everyone, including children. Through their behavior and actions, children reveal Nature’s secrets, and we can learn valuable lessons from observing them.

natureAsATeacher.summary: Nature itself is a powerful teacher. It constantly imparts lessons to us through everyday experiences, people, and activities. Those who are attentive learn and progress, while those who ignore these teachings face problems and suffering.

roleOfGuru.summary: A Guru is someone who imparts knowledge to others. Every Guru was once a student (sishya). From time immemorial, Gurus have been teaching spiritual lessons to humanity, culminating in the Vedas and Upanishads as compiled by Vyas Bhagvan.

continuousTeachingAndLearning.summary: Learning is an ongoing process. Before Vyas, teachings existed, and they have continued after him. By reflecting on everything around us—trees, earth, air, sun, moon, people, and actions—we can uncover Nature's secrets and apply them to our lives.

understandingOthersFeelings.summary: Hinduism is not just a religion; it is a culture that teaches the principles needed for a better life. Life operates within a triangle of nature, society, and self. Respecting the feelings and needs of others is key to harmony, peace, and happiness.

respectingSelfAndSociety.summary: Understanding the value of oneself and the purpose of one's birth is crucial. Developing consciousness towards this purpose helps foster harmony and well-being, while neglecting it leads to problems and suffering.

secretsOfNatureAndTheMind.summary: Religions and sciences alike seek to understand the secrets of Nature, the human mind, and the connection between the individual and society. While scientists use instruments to extend their senses, spiritual teachings reveal deeper truths beyond sensory perception.

relationshipBetweenTotalityAndSelf.summary: Atma Cyan (self-realization) seeks to understand the relationship between the Totality (Brahman or the Universal Being) and the individual. Though man is a fraction of the Totality, he remains intrinsically connected to Nature and is a part of it.

legacyOfGurus.summary: Our ancient Gurus have imparted deep wisdom about the secrets of Nature and the universe. We honor and bow our heads to these Gurus who have lived before us, recognizing the value of their teachings.

angerAndMentalFrequency.summary: Anger is a universal trait seen in all creatures. When we get angry, our mental frequency increases to 25-30 cycles per second, which wastes our life force. This causes an increase in the spinning speed of life-force particles, leading to their loss from the body. This depletion leaves the angry person tired and weak.

impactOnTheBody.summary: During anger, life-force particles expand beyond the body and are lost. This results in tiredness, confusion, and a loss of control over thoughts and actions. Additionally, blood pressure rises, and the heart, nerves, and muscles are strained, which can cause long-term damage.

angerAndRelationships.summary: Anger mostly affects those closest to us—often those who love and support us. This unfairly damages relationships with our loved ones. Over time, habitual anger can cause kith and kin to avoid us, isolating us from those who care the most.

angerAsTheRootOfAllSins.summary: Anger is described as the root of all sins in ancient Tamil poetry. It isolates individuals, leads to personal failure, and destroys relationships. It is crucial to practice neutralizing anger to prevent it from taking control of our lives.

neutralizingAnger.summary: At Meditation centers, training is offered to neutralize unwanted anger. However, only by practicing these methods daily can one achieve results. Individuals are encouraged to list the people they often get angry with and practice controlling their anger towards them, starting with the most frequent person and progressing gradually.

husbandWifeRelationship.summary: The husband-wife relationship is unique in its depth and union of souls. It is especially important to avoid letting anger harm this special bond. Reflecting on the love, care, and comfort in this relationship can help prevent anger from damaging it.

practicalExerciseForAngerControl.title: Practical Exercise for Anger Control
practicalExerciseForAngerControl.description: Individuals are advised to take a pledge not to let anger hurt the body or mind of their loved ones. Practicing self-restraint for 10 minutes daily, especially after meditation, helps in controlling anger. Begin with the person most affected by your anger, and gradually move on to others.

practiceAndAwareness.title: Practice & Awareness
practiceAndAwareness.message: Success in anger management requires concrete practice through writing, analyzing, and pledging. Reading or hearing about these methods alone is not enough; daily practice with awareness is key to neutralizing anger and achieving success.

principle1.description: Each person must live by the earnings made through his or her own mental or physical labor.

details.summary: No one should take the possessions of others. Everyone has their own needs, and fulfilling them must be done through personal effort. If one cannot fulfill their needs through honest labor, resorting to another's possessions will lead to a life resembling that of animals.

comparisonWithAnimals.summary: Animals, especially carnivores, rely on killing for survival, performing four actions: torturing, killing, claiming, and destroying freedom. These are considered sinful for humans and must be avoided.
actions: Violently claiming its body as food

geneticCenter.summary: Human beings, like carnivores, have inherited these tendencies through the genetic center. These four sinful actions must be changed through conscious effort, using one's body and mind to live a divine life.

principle2.description: Our method of living should not cause any suffering to the body or mind of any person.

details.summary: Nature does not cause suffering; humans do. If everyone follows this principle and avoids causing pain to others, society would live in peace.

principle3.description: One should not kill any living being for food.

details.summary: This principle reiterates the point made in the First Principle. Killing for food is a sinful act that should be avoided.

principle4.description: One must have the utmost respect for the possessions and freedom of others and help to protect them.

details.summary: This principle calls for the removal of exploitation in human society. Respecting others' possessions and freedom is fundamental to a peaceful coexistence.

principle5.description: One must cultivate loving kindness and strive to alleviate the miseries of others to the extent possible.

details.summary: Society functions through cooperation and help. Cultivating kindness and helping others will lead to overall happiness.

conclusion.summary: All adults and thinkers should adopt and follow this five-fold moral culture in life. Spreading this code of conduct should be considered a sacred human obligation.

definition.title: Definition of Religion
definition.summary: Religion is the science of living, providing a safe method of living with principles derived from the experiences of mankind.

details.title: Explanation
details.explanation: Men of wisdom have selected important activities and enjoyments compatible with prevailing cultural values based on time, place, and environmental conditions. They have categorized do's and don'ts for the benefit and safety of people in their living processes and relationships.

culturalValues.title: Cultural Values
culturalValues.roots: The world-wide cultural values of mankind stem from the evolutionary process of Nature and the experiences of countless generations.
culturalValues.metaphor: In the ocean of cultural values, each religion is an island defined by its own time, place, and environmental conditions.

guidance.title: Guidance of Religion
guidance.summary: Religion serves as the only guiding light for mankind to live successfully and peacefully, maintaining harmonious relationships with fellow beings.

details.title: Core Principles
details.observation: There are several religions worldwide, differing peripherally and ritualistically.

realisationOfGod.title: Realization of God
realisationOfGod.summary: To fully benefit from religion, followers must realize God to their satisfaction and follow virtues responsibly, emerging from their own psycho-physical character.

details.title: Interconnection
details.interconnection: Worship of God and a virtuous way of life are interlinked; virtuous deeds arise from the light of the realization of God.

content.paragraph: The teachings of great men and philosophers can be compared to the dress of a child. When we stitch a dress for a child, we stitch it in a bigger size as we expect the child to grow. Initially the dress may not be very fit, but within a few months, the growth of the child will make the dress of correct size.
Similarly, when philosophers preach to society, the people may not accept their preaching and refuse it, thinking that it is not suitable and required for them.

Philosophers have knowledge about the past, present, and future. In this 'thirikalagnanam' (knowledge of the three times), they express their teachings for the betterment and peace of society. Their ideals and plans may seem unnecessary to common people who are living with their own crooked ideals and views.
Only good thinkers and time can explain the greatness of those teachings. Until then, those teachings will be neglected like an oversized dress.

list.intellectualGuidance: Living under the guidance of intellectuals
list.womensRights: Respecting Womanhood and giving full equal rights
list.natureLaw: Living in tune with the Law of Nature
list.sportsForChildren: Sports to be made non-commercial and only for the children
list.causeEffectEducation: The educational curriculum to include teaching the Law of Cause and Effect
list.foodWaterAvailability: Food and water to be available for each person of the world
list.universalTruth: Universal agreement on Truth (God) to bring about One World Religion acceptable by all.

paragraphs: In general, people do not care much about the things which are obtained by simple and easy means. That is quite the nature of human mind. We give respect and importance to the property which is greater value or belonging to others. We, therefore, devote almost all our efforts and energy in procuring those things. We should have a mind, broad to go far beyond that which we can achieve.

For this, we should introspect and plan accordingly. We should realise 'What I have'? We have legs, hands, pleasures, wife, children, relations, house to live in, and occupation to earn and so on. We have sufficient or sometimes even surplus with us. Then, why do we expect more from God?

Expectation makes us only beggars. This expectation is the root cause for various problems and chaos in day to day life. Nature has provided us with excellent talents and will power. We should develop these talents and powers by means of which we can help and guide others. We must find the cause and effect in our own efforts. This is 'Karma Yoga'.

We spent most of our life span worrying about others and not contented with what we have. That is the main course for the problems throughout the world. So, only spirituality can solve the problems of mankind. Expectation will only keep us in deficiency and dependence and we feel ourselves to be in penury.

God has gifted us the physical body along with life to enjoy. Instead of being thankful and grateful to Nature, we go on demanding this and that from Almighty. Maharishi says 'Give up expectations for 30 days and see the result after achieving the fruit of the result, our mind will automatically give up its efficiency on expectation.

So, when one comes to the non-expecting stage, he gets the wonderful opportunity to utilise his powers and get satisfaction. Without expecting anything from others, we should be broad minded and help others with what we have either physically or financially or mentally etc. The only way to maintain harmony and friendly relation is to move with humanity and gratitude towards both the animate and inanimate things.

We should not by any means develop hatred feelings. Therefore, the only solution for this is to bless the hatred in the meditations we do both in the morning and evening. Blessing, Blessing, Blessing between one turns hatred, lovable. By following this, one's life turns harmonious. This is quite possible. Only thing is we should wish it and try.

So, by the grace of the Divine, one should try to fulfill his own needs maximum by himself with the use of thought, word and deed. When all this becomes possible, 'Where is the necessity for us to expect from others'? Thus, we come to a clear concept that we are the one and only person responsible for hatred towards others and not anyone else.

Particularly in SKY, there is no way of developing such hatred feelings, because in SKY, we train our mind to attain spiritual consciousness which broadens the mind. When mind gets broadened, love and compassion comes out whole heartedly as treasure. This way of living is 'Karmayoga'.

articles.title: CAUSE OF PAIN AND PROBLEMS
articles.author: Maharishi
articles.desc: According to the developed characters in the body and mind, whatever waves emerge from the deeds, thoughts and experiences which are conflicting with the natural functioning order within and without, those waves result in contamination of the genetic center...

articles.title: Better to be healthy than wealthy
articles.author: Maharishi
articles.desc: Physical exercises are very very important for mankind. In the olden days, people did not give importance to physical exercise. The reason was that they had enough physical labour. So, they were able to maintain a healthy body and did not care much about the physical exercises. Even women were taught classical’ dances and for men sports were encouraged. What this prevalence and usage show?

articles.title: The Third Eye & A Thousand Petals in Our Brian
articles.author: Maharishi
articles.desc: he sixth centre is the Agna chakra having its seat in the region between the eyebrow sand is related to the our life-force. It is linked with the Pituitary gland. The word 'Agna' means control, administration. This centre controls the sensual activities.

articles.title: TEACHINGS OF PHILOSOPHERS
articles.author: Maharishi
articles.desc: The teachings of great men and philosophers can be compared to the dress of a child. When we stitch dress for a child, we stitch it in a bigger size as we expect the child to grow. Initially the dress may not be very fit, but within a few months, the growth of the child will make the dress of correct size.

articles.title: VICTORY IS IN YOUR HANDS
articles.author: Maharishi
articles.desc: In general, people do not care much about the things which are obtained by simple and easy means. That is quite the nature of human mind. We give respect and importance to the property which is greater value or belonging to others. We, therefore, devote almost all our efforts and energy in procuring those things. We should have a mind, broad to go far beyond that which we can achieve.

articles.title: ANGER KILLS KIN AN KITH
articles.author: Maharishi
articles.desc: When we get angry our mental frequency shoots up to 25-30 cycles per second. Because, of this raise, our life force is wasted. In its effort to replenish, the functioning state of Almighty causes an increase in the spinning speed of life force particles. Because, then, additional bio-magnetic force would be produced. Increase in the spin causes increase in the distance between two particles.

articles.title: YOGA THE SCIENCE OF LIVING
articles.author: Maharishi
articles.desc: Yoga is a system to make a man `a real man` to enjoy the life happily, peacefully and blissfully. The purpose of the life of man is very great and noble. It is to develop the consciousness to the fullness. Yoga is to make the method of living in unison with the purpose of life.

articles.title: The universal field contains various mixtures of five elements or Pancha Bhoodas
articles.author: Maharishi
articles.desc: The Akash particles is the repository of all the secrets of nature and is the source of all sciences prevailing among mankind.The universal field contains various mixtures of five elements

articles.title: SCIENCE of KAYA KALPA
articles.author: Maharishi
articles.desc: Ever since man started curing illness, he began to discover the causes for illness. Then prevention of illness also was added in the evolution of culture. While he was enjoying pleasures and suffering from pains through his five senses, through his sixth sense he started to understand the perfect functional order of nature, i.e. the principle of cause and effect.

articles.title: FIVE FOLD MORAL CULTURE
articles.author: Maharishi
articles.desc: There should simply not be any question of taking another person’s possessions.  Everyone has his needs.  If he cannot fulfill these by this own earning, it becomes necessary for them to make use of someone else’s hard-earned possessions.  If this is allowed, eventually human life will start resembling animal life.Animals do not have the capacity to produce the food stuff that they need to satisfy hunger.  Most of them therefore depend for their food on killing and eating other animals.

articles.title: IMPORTANCE OF RELIGION
articles.author: Maharishi
articles.desc: Religion is the science of living. It is a safe method of living, with principles of life selected from the experiences of mankind. According to the time, place and environmental conditions, the men of wisdom selected some important activities and enjoyments of life,' compatible with the prevailing cultural values.
